original_interpretation: Global semiconductor sales rose 25.6% to US$791.7 billion in 2025 (SIA, WSTS data).
evidence_found: "global semiconductor sales hit $791.7 billion in 2025, an increase of 25.6% compared to the 2024 total of $630.5 billion" (SIA release, 6 Feb 2026, para 1). WSTS Spring 2026 table (2 Jun 2026): "Total World - $M 795,640 ... 26.2" (2025).
correction: SIA's Feb 2026 first estimate was later revised by WSTS to US$795.6bn (+26.2%) for 2025 (WSTS Spring 2026 release). See new superseding claim.
notes: Source supports the claim as SIA's initial figure; WSTS's later annual total is the current figure (same as CLM-0030).

original_interpretation: SIA reports memory sales of US$223.1 billion in 2025, up 34.8%.
evidence_found: "Memory products were second in terms of sales, increasing by 34.8% in 2024 to a total of $223.1 billion." (SIA release, 6 Feb 2026, product segments para). WSTS Spring 2026 table: "Memory 230,042 ... 39.0" (2025).
correction: The '2024' in SIA's sentence is a typo for 2025 (2024 memory was US$165.1bn per SIA's Feb 2025 release). WSTS later revised 2025 memory to US$230.0bn (+39.0%). See superseding claim.
notes: Typo confirmed: SIA Feb 2025 release states memory 'increasing by 78.9% in 2024 to a total of $165.1 billion', so the US$223.1bn figure is 2025. Consistent with CLM-0036.

original_interpretation: US semiconductor industry R&D spending was US$70.0 billion in 2024, and annual R&D has exceeded 15% of sales for 24 years.
evidence_found: 2025 SIA Factbook: "In 2024, total U.S. semiconductor industry investment in R&D totaled $70.0 billion." (p. 16); "Annual R&D expenditures as a percent of sales have exceeded 15 percent over the past 24 years." (p. 17). SIA 2026 State of the Industry: "American semiconductor companies spent $76.8 billion on R&D in 2025, up from $69.6 billion in 2024" (p. 14).
correction: Newer data: US$76.8bn of R&D in 2025 (SIA 2026 report, citing the 2026 Factbook), and 2024 is restated there as US$69.6bn. See superseding claim.
notes: Both parts were correctly quoted from the 2025 Factbook. Note the Factbook's chart heading says 'over the past 20 years' while the body says '24 years'. Whether the >15% streak held in 2025 was not confirmed from a source opened this run.

original_interpretation: US semiconductor industry gross capex was US$49.5 billion in 2024, and annual capex has averaged 10-15% of sales over 20 years.
evidence_found: "The U.S. semiconductor industry gross capital expenditures were $49.5 billion in 2024." (2025 SIA Factbook, p. 14-15); "ANNUAL CAPITAL EXPENDITURES AS A PERCENT OF SALES HAVE AVERAGED BETWEEN 10 AND 15 PERCENT OVER THE PAST 20 YEARS. Annual capital expenditures as a percent of sales have exceeded 10 percent in all but 2 of the past 20 years." (p. 15)
notes: No 2025 capex figure found in the SIA 2026 State of the Industry report; the 2026 Factbook PDF was not located, so a newer capex figure may exist.

original_interpretation: SIA states that the US industry's R&D and capex as a share of sales have generally not fluctuated with market cyclicality.
evidence_found: "Investment levels in terms of share of sales have generally not been subject to fluctuations associated with market cyclicality." (2025 SIA Factbook, Section 3 intro, p. 13)
notes: Correctly typed as reported_claim (industry body's own characterisation).

original_interpretation: Worldwide semiconductor manufacturing equipment billings rose 15% to US$135.1 billion in 2025, with China the largest market at US$49.3 billion.
evidence_found: "Worldwide sales of semiconductor manufacturing equipment increased 15% to $135.1 billion in 2025 from $117.1 billion in 2024"; "spending in China remained near record levels at $49.3 billion, down just 0.5% from the prior year" (SEMI release, 7 Apr 2026)
notes: China is the largest region listed (Taiwan US$31.5bn, Korea US$25.8bn). Population = billings reported by SEMI and SEAJ members (WWSEMS). Q1 2026 data (US$36.55bn) exists but does not supersede the 2025 annual total.

original_interpretation: TSMC reported 2025 net revenue of NT$3,809.05 billion, up 31.6% from 2024.
evidence_found: "Net revenue was NT$3,809.05 billion, representing a 31.6% increase from 2024." (4Q25 Management Report, p. 1, Full Year 2025)
notes: 20-F revenue-by-geography table total for 2025: NT$3,809,054 million, consistent.

original_interpretation: TSMC's 2025 gross margin was 59.9%, up from 56.1% in 2024.
evidence_found: "Gross margin was 59.9%, up 3.8 percentage points from 56.1% in 2024." (4Q25 Management Report, p. 1); table: "Gross Margin 62.3% 59.5% 59.0% 59.9% 56.1%" (p. 3)

original_interpretation: High Performance Computing accounted for 58% of TSMC's 2025 net revenue, smartphones 29%.
evidence_found: "Net Revenue by Platform 2025 2024 / High Performance Computing 58% 51% / Smartphone 29% 35%" (4Q25 Management Report, p. 2)
notes: 20-F platform table: HPC NT$2,192,931m and Smartphone NT$1,110,816m of NT$3,809,054m (57.6% / 29.2%), consistent with rounded shares.

original_interpretation: Global semiconductor sales fell 8.2% to US$526.8 billion in 2023 (SIA, WSTS data).
evidence_found: "global semiconductor industry sales totaled $526.8 billion in 2023, a decrease of 8.2% compared to the 2022 total of $574.1 billion" (SIA release, 5 Feb 2024, para 1)
notes: Initial SIA figure; SIA's Feb 2025 release repeats '2023 total of $526.8 billion'. Other atlas claims cite a later WSTS series value of ~US$526.9bn (immaterial).

original_interpretation: Memory sales were US$92.3 billion in 2023 (SIA, WSTS data).
evidence_found: "Memory products were second in terms of sales, totaling $92.3 billion." (SIA release, 5 Feb 2024, product segments para)

original_interpretation: TSMC, as a foundry, manufactures semiconductors for customers using its own processes on integrated circuit designs provided by those customers.
evidence_found: "As a foundry, we manufacture semiconductors using our manufacturing processes for our customers based on proprietary integrated circuit designs provided by them." (2025 Form 20-F, Item 4, Business Overview of the Company)
notes: SRC-0077 (investor.tsmc.com PDF) opened via web_extract but text was truncated before this passage; passage located in the same 20-F on SEC EDGAR (SRC-0825, tsm-20251231.htm, filed 2026-04-16).

original_interpretation: TSMC's 2025 capital expenditures were NT$1,272,411 million (US$40,895 million).
evidence_found: "Our capital expenditures in 2023, 2024 and 2025 were NT$ 949,817 million, NT$ 956,007 million and NT$ 1,272,411 million (US$ 40,895 million, translated from a weighted average exchange rate of NT$ 31.11 to US$1.00), respectively." (20-F, Item 4); 4Q25 MR p. 7: "US$40.90 billion for the year"
notes: SRC-0077 (investor.tsmc.com PDF) opened via web_extract but text was truncated before this passage; passage located in the same 20-F on SEC EDGAR (SRC-0825, tsm-20251231.htm, filed 2026-04-16). 20-F also guides 2026 capex of US$52-56bn.

original_interpretation: TSMC's 2025 capital expenditures equalled roughly 33% of its 2025 net revenue (NT$1,272.4bn / NT$3,809.05bn).
evidence_found: Inputs re-checked: capex NT$1,272,411m (20-F) and net revenue NT$3,809,054m (20-F geography table) / NT$3,809.05bn (4Q25 MR p. 1). 1,272,411 / 3,809,054 = 33.4%.
notes: Arithmetic correct; both figures NT$, same period (CY2025). TSMC-only ratio, as the claim's population says.

original_interpretation: TSMC's largest customer accounted for 19% of its 2025 net revenue (25% in 2023, 22% in 2024).
evidence_found: "Our largest customer in 2023, 2024 and 2025 accounted for 25%, 22% and 19% of our net revenue in the respective year." (20-F, Item 3 risk factors)
notes: Found in both the investor.tsmc.com PDF extract and the EDGAR copy. Same passage: second-largest customer 11%, 12%, 17%; top ten 70%, 76%, 78%.

original_interpretation: Customers headquartered in North America accounted for 75% of TSMC's 2025 net revenue (NT$2,875,270 million).
evidence_found: "We categorize our net revenue mainly based on the countries where our customers are headquartered..."; table: "North America 1,470,215 68% 2,031,326 70% 2,875,270 75%" (20-F, Item 4, Markets and Customers)
notes: SRC-0077 (investor.tsmc.com PDF) opened via web_extract but text was truncated before this passage; passage located in the same 20-F on SEC EDGAR (SRC-0825, tsm-20251231.htm, filed 2026-04-16). Geography basis confirmed as customer headquarters, not shipment destination.

original_interpretation: Some TSMC customers pay 'temporary receipts' (advance payments) to retain specified capacity at TSMC fabs, later refunded or offset against receivables by mutual consent.
evidence_found: "some of our customers have entered into agreements with us to pay temporary receipts in order to retain specified capacity at our fabs. The treatment of advance temporary receipts, either by refund or by accounts receivable offsetting, will be determined by mutual consent when the terms and conditions set forth in the agreements are satisfied." (20-F, Item 4)
notes: SRC-0077 (investor.tsmc.com PDF) opened via web_extract but text was truncated before this passage; passage located in the same 20-F on SEC EDGAR (SRC-0825, tsm-20251231.htm, filed 2026-04-16).

original_interpretation: TSMC's 2025 annual capacity exceeded 17 million 12-inch equivalent wafers.
evidence_found: "In 2025, our annual capacity (in 12-inch equivalent wafers) exceeded 17 million wafers, compared to approximately 17 million wafers in 2024." (20-F, Item 4, Manufacturing Capacity)
notes: SRC-0077 (investor.tsmc.com PDF) opened via web_extract but text was truncated before this passage; passage located in the same 20-F on SEC EDGAR (SRC-0825, tsm-20251231.htm, filed 2026-04-16).

original_interpretation: TSMC Arizona agreed incentives with the U.S. Department of Commerce under the CHIPS Act of up to US$6.6 billion in direct funding and up to US$5 billion of proposed loans.
evidence_found: "In November 2024, TSMC Arizona Corporation ('TSMC Arizona') entered into agreements with the U.S. Department of Commerce for the receipt of certain incentives pursuant to the U.S. CHIPS Act, which includes up to US$6.6 billion in total direct funding and up to US$5 billion of proposed loans." (20-F, Item 3)
notes: Found in both copies. Agreement dated November 2024; amounts are maxima, not disbursements.

original_interpretation: Germany agreed up to EUR 5 billion of state aid to ESMC (TSMC's Dresden joint venture with Bosch, Infineon and NXP) under the European Chips Act, approved by the European Commission.
evidence_found: 20-F: "In December 2024, ESMC, our subsidiary in Germany, entered into an agreement with the Federal Republic of Germany for the receipt of up to EUR5 billion state aid under the European Chips Act (Regulation (EU) 2023/1781)." EC page title: "Commission approves €5 billion German State aid measure to support ESMC"; "ESMC is a joint venture between ... ('TSMC'), Bosch, Infineon, and NXP."
notes: Timeline: EC approval Aug 2024; aid agreement signed Dec 2024. 20-F: Bosch, Infineon and NXP each hold 10% (TSMC 70%).

original_interpretation: NVIDIA's fiscal 2026 revenue was US$215.9 billion, up 65%.
evidence_found: "Fiscal year revenue was a record $215.9 billion, up 65% from a year ago." (CFO Commentary Q4 FY26, Revenue section); table: "Revenue $215,938 $130,497 65%"
notes: Note: SRC-0078 is an 8-K exhibit (EX-99.2); company_filing type is acceptable.

original_interpretation: NVIDIA's fiscal 2026 GAAP gross margin was 71.1%.
evidence_found: Fiscal 2026 Summary (GAAP) table: "Gross margin 71.1 % 75.0 % (3.9) pts" (CFO Commentary Q4 FY26)

original_interpretation: At the end of fiscal 2026 NVIDIA's total supply-related commitments were US$95.2 billion.
evidence_found: "Inventory was $21.4 billion, up from $19.8 billion sequentially, and total supply-related commitments were $95.2 billion." (CFO Commentary Q4 FY26, balance sheet section)
notes: Point-in-time figure as of 25 Jan 2026; later quarterly figures (FY27) not checked.

original_interpretation: NVIDIA had US$27.0 billion of multi-year cloud service agreements at the end of fiscal 2026.
evidence_found: "Multi-year cloud service agreements were $27.0 billion, up from $26.0 billion sequentially, to support the growing needs of our research and development efforts." (CFO Commentary Q4 FY26)
notes: The researcher's note ('buying capacity back from cloud providers') goes beyond the source: NVIDIA says the agreements support its R&D needs.

original_interpretation: NVIDIA held US$21.4 billion of inventory at the end of fiscal 2026.
evidence_found: "Inventory was $21.4 billion, up from $19.8 billion sequentially" (CFO Commentary Q4 FY26)
notes: As of end FY2026 (25 Jan 2026).

original_interpretation: NVIDIA uses a fabless and contract-manufacturing strategy, relying on partners for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing and packaging.
evidence_found: "We utilize a fabless and contracting manufacturing strategy, whereby we employ and partner with key suppliers for all phases of the manufacturing process, including wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging." (FY2026 10-K, Item 1, Manufacturing)
notes: Read from full EDGAR HTML (web_extract output was truncated).

original_interpretation: NVIDIA uses TSMC and Samsung as foundries to produce its semiconductor wafers.
evidence_found: "We utilize foundries, such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited, or TSMC, and Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd., or Samsung, to produce our semiconductor wafers." (FY2026 10-K, Item 1, Manufacturing)
notes: 'such as' means not an exhaustive list.

original_interpretation: To secure supply and capacity NVIDIA has paid premiums, provided deposits and entered long-term supply agreements and capacity commitments, which increased its product costs.
evidence_found: "To secure future supply and capacity, we have paid premiums, provided deposits, and entered into long-term supply agreements and capacity commitments, which have increased our product costs and this may continue." (FY2026 10-K, Item 1A)

original_interpretation: In growth periods NVIDIA may place non-cancellable inventory orders ahead of normal lead times, pay premiums or provide deposits to secure supply.
evidence_found: "In periods of growth, we may place non-cancellable inventory orders for certain product components in advance of our historical lead times, pay premiums, or provide deposits to secure future supply and capacity and may need to continue to do so." (FY2026 10-K, Item 1, Manufacturing)

original_interpretation: Qualcomm's per-unit patent royalties are generally a percentage of the licensee's wholesale selling price of complete licensed products, net of permissible deductions, with some products subject to per-unit minimums and/or caps.
evidence_found: "Per-unit royalties are generally based upon a percentage of the wholesale (i.e., licensee's) selling price of complete licensed products, net of certain permissible deductions (including transportation, insurance, packing costs and other items), with certain products subject to per unit minimums and/or per unit caps." (FY2025 10-K, Item 1, QTL)
notes: Read from full EDGAR HTML.

original_interpretation: Qualcomm's licensees pay royalties quarterly based on their sales of products using its licensed IP.
evidence_found: "QTL licensing revenues consist primarily of per-unit royalties. Licensees pay quarterly royalties based on their sales of products incorporating or using our licensed intellectual property." (FY2025 10-K, Item 1, QTL)

original_interpretation: Qualcomm's chip business (QCT) is mostly fabless, using TSMC, Samsung and GlobalFoundries as primary foundries and ASE, Amkor, SPIL and STATSChipPAC for assembly and test.
evidence_found: "Other than for certain of our RFFE modules and RF filter products, QCT utilizes a fabless production model"; "The primary foundry suppliers ... include Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), Samsung Electronics and Global Foundries. Our primary semiconductor assembly and test suppliers are Advanced Semiconductor Engineering, Amkor Technology, Siliconware Precision Industries and STATSChipPAC." (FY2025 10-K, Item 1)
notes: 'Mostly' fabless is fair: RFFE modules and RF filters are the stated exceptions.

original_interpretation: Synopsys sells EDA software mainly as network licences, including time-based licences bundled with support (subscriptions) and perpetual licences sold with support.
evidence_found: "The majority of licenses to our EDA products and Ansys semiconductor products are network licenses..."; "Our S&A software solutions are offered as subscription solutions and also as perpetual licenses. Software subscription arrangements include bundles of time-based software licenses..." (10-K Item 1); "EDA products and services are typically sold through Technology Subscription License (TSL) arrangements" (MD&A)
correction: Network-licence part verified for EDA. The subscription and perpetual wording describes S&A (Ansys) software, not EDA; EDA is typically sold via TSL contracts of generally 2-3 years. See superseding claim.
notes: Researcher's ellipsis joined sentences about different product groups.

original_interpretation: Synopsys charges design-IP licence fees typically per design, plus royalties in some cases.
evidence_found: "We typically license Synopsys IP products under nonexclusive license agreements that provide usage rights for a specific number of designs. Fees under these licenses are typically charged on a per design basis plus, in some cases, royalties." (FY2025 10-K, Item 1)

original_interpretation: Synopsys depends on a relatively small number of large customers, and challenges at a major foundry customer hurt its fiscal 2025 results.
evidence_found: "Further, we depend on a relatively small number of large customers for a large portion of our revenues. For example, challenges with a major foundry customer negatively impacted our financial results for fiscal year 2025." (FY2025 10-K, Item 1A)
notes: Company risk-factor disclosure; the foundry customer is not named in this passage.
